lines.text: The long way round, then.
KETTLE NOTCH 5, cut deep in the face toward home.
The far face says KETTLE NOTCH too. The number under it has been scratched out.
Well. It isn't wrong.
Sit. It's free.
Eldwin sleeps by the fire. Once in the night he wakes, and Jasper is still sitting up, watching the road they came by, humming something under his breath. It has a lantern in it, somewhere.
When he wakes again it's first light, the kettle's on, and Jasper looks as if he never slept.
There you are.
The cold is coming through the gap like water through a split barrel.
That's not right. Easy, now. Easy.
The stones lying in the gap stand up.
The last stone grinds back into its place. It sits crooked, and the frost behind it stops.
That'll keep until someone who knows what he's doing has a look at it.
Here the wall is laid tight and true, every stone hearted, and one small gap left low, facing north.
Somebody's been keeping this. Properly.
The stone is cold, and doesn't answer.
Asleep. Well. You've earned it.
The goose's takings, in a heap on the gravel: a battered felt hat, a pair of spectacles, a silver thimble, a cooper's mallet, a great many crusts, and one brass button.
He did well for himself.
That's my hat.
She puts it on, and for once says nothing about anything.
There. Now I can see who I'm talking to.
He looks at Eldwin for a while.
Thought you'd be younger, from the voice.
Most people do.
Come on, Patience. Letters won't carry themselves.
My mother's thimble. I'd turned the house over twice.
She puts it on at once, though she has nothing to sew.
Reuben goes down the barrel wall tapping each barrel with it, and listening.
Sound. Every one.
He's still a goose.
I'm afraid so.
Then it's the other one. The white one. She's the one who's enchanted.
Did he leave any of my crusts?
I'm afraid not.
Good. Then he liked them.
Not mine. I don't lose buttons.
That beaver's started on her. Down by the roots, south side.
If he drops her, nobody broke any rule. That's how I'd look at it, if I were a worse man.
And are you?
I'm thinking about it.
Fresh tooth marks round the foot of the pine, and chips everywhere. Eldwin lays a hand on the bark, and feels the wall go thin, a long way off.
Not this one.
He's gone back to his dam. Took a birch with him, out of spite.
I'll leave her standing. I'll tell my boy to leave her standing.
Will you tell him why?
I'll tell him I don't know. That's what I was told.
Forty-two. She's gone over the wall. Gyp's been looking at that stile all morning.
Shall I fetch her?
I'd not go over there myself. That side's not mine.
The ewe is standing in the frost with her back to the wind, as if she'd been waiting for somebody sensible.
Come on, then. Home.
Forty-three.
Gyp sits down, which is the most she'll say.
You went right over. Was it cold?
Colder than this side.
My father always said.
